This was another big goal, partly related to trying to get the 3D work into the hands of external assets, and partly a specific exercise in combining elements.

The main element to be combined was Survival of the Fittest, which had to form the character ‘body’, but was much too big to fit into the small corridor. A sort of 2.5D conversion in ‘real time’, such that this ‘unborn baby’ can go hand in hand with existing content, but also have a look and feel which doesn’t belong to the same game (or at least not entirely).

The other main ingredient is 3D HUD elements, which give a visual representation of the situation. This might be very well something to look at with a friend or let’s play on the go. Thus the design has to match a specific look and feel, with little bells and whistles. This was the initial point, see the initial sketches:

The idea was that this becomes a sort of alien spaceship visualization with alien elements, because that part of the design is very close to ‘design as seen in the original game’. These were the base sketches:
